subject: Order form: scoped training exclusion & feedback-license negotiation
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@lumera.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Lumera AI Procurement <procurement@lumera.ai>
Date: 2025-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Order form redline: training exclusion and feedback license

Diego —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Attached is our latest redline to the order form (Lumera_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). Two priority asks from our side that we want to close this week: 1) a narrow training exclusion so our sensitive customer transcripts never become training material; and 2) clarity on the feedback license — we want to be sure telemetry/feedback used for product improvement cannot be used to claim ownership over Lumera outputs or be sold.

High level questions: can Redwood agree to a production-only training exclusion (production logs + annotated PII removal), and accept a feedback license limited to aggregated, de-identified metrics (no downstream productization)?

Alex
Head of Procurement — Lumera AI

Attachment: Lumera_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@lumera.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline: training exclusion and feedback license

Alex — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're aligned on the goal: protect Lumera's customer content while keeping a narrow path for ops/quality tooling. A few items we need from your side to get legal/eng unstuck: 1) sample data flow that shows where "production logs" land (S3 path / Kinesis / PubSub) and retention windows; 2) confirmation on who (internal Lumera teams) can tag content as "sensitive" versus a default opt-out; 3) any internal classification rules you already use for PII removal so our preprocessing team can estimate effort.

I'm looping Laura to propose redline language and Marissa for procurement cadence. I added inline notes in diego_redline_notes.docx — mostly technical questions and two proposed compromise bullets.

Proposed next steps: Laura to share suggested MSA exhibit language today; engineering (karthik) to confirm feasibility of short-lived KV retention for QA-only telemetry; target legal response for Lumera by EOD Wednesday.

—Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: diego_redline_notes.docx

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Alex Park <alex.park@lumera.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-12T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline: training exclusion and feedback license

Alex / Diego —

Thanks for the context. I've drafted a short exhibit to the MSA that attempts to capture Lumera's protections while leaving Redwood a constrained path for operational improvements. Key points in the proposed snippet (see MSA_ExhibitA_proposed_snippet.txt):

- Training exclusion: Redwood will not use any Lumera customer content (defined as content generated by or uploaded to Lumera production accounts) to further train or fine-tune models used in Redwood's hosted offerings, except where Lumera has expressly opted-in in writing. Operational telemetry (e.g., anonymized latency/quality metrics) may be retained for performance monitoring only, subject to a 90‑day automatic purge.

- Feedback license: Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use aggregated, de-identified feedback and metrics to improve the service. Aggregated means metrics that cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct customer prompts or outputs. No rights are granted to sell or sublicense Lumera output or to include Lumera-derived prompts/outputs in models that are externally distributed.

Open items we still need evidence for (Diego's ask):
1) Data flow diagram for production ingestion (where the content lands and which services access it).
2) Evidence of automated PII removal (or the ability to add a pre-ingest filter).
3) Retention configuration for any KV/prefix caches and whether we can set a 90-day lifecycle for Lumera accounts.

If Lumera can provide (1)-(3) by EOD Tuesday, I can incorporate the wording into the order form redline and provide guidance to procurement on the acceptance checklist.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Park <alex.park@lumera.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-13T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline: training exclusion and feedback license

Laura — appreciate the clear draft. A couple of asks/clarifications from Lumera: 1) Can the 90-day purge be shortened to 30 days for any KV/prefix cache data? Our security team prefers shorter windows for sensitive workloads. 2) For "aggregated metrics" please confirm that embeddings or vector representations derived from customer content are excluded. We want to avoid a scenario where derivative vectors become part of model improvements.

Operational ask: would Redwood consider a limited "non-commercial A/B test" exception that allows Redwood to include de-identified derivative outputs for internal A/B testing (no external distribution) for up to 90 days, with Lumera approval per experiment? This helps both parties validate quality without granting productization rights.

We attached our DPA template (Lumera_DPA_template.pdf) and can upload a small data-flow diagram if you prefer GDrive.

Regards,
Alex

Attachment: Lumera_DPA_template.pdf

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@lumera.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-13T11:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redline: training exclusion and feedback license

Alex — all reasonable asks. Quick operational take: Karthik, can we support a 30-day lifecycle for KV/prefix cache entries for Lumera accounts? Also can the engineering team guarantee that embeddings/vectors generated during customer sessions are never persisted beyond session scope unless explicitly allowed?

Laura — if we tighten the KV lifecycle to 30 days and add a per-experiment Lumera approval clause for the limited A/B testing path (internal only, no external distribution, experiment runbook to be shared), would Lumera be comfortable with the proposed language? If so, I can push the updated order form and DocuSign link this afternoon.

Next steps / timeline:
- Lumera to confirm A/B experiment approval flow and provide data-flow diagram (EOD tomorrow).
- Karthik to confirm feasibility (timeline: 48h).
- Laura to finalize exhibit language once technical constraints confirmed.
- Marissa to prepare procurement DocuSign once redline accepted.

Thanks — I want to get this across the line this week.

—Diego
